statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-96959 (GHSA-c399-9853-6jmj, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c399-9853-6jmj): unbounded resource allocation in signed-XML processing that leads to denial of service. Affected: System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 10.0.0 to 10.0.12, fixed in 10.0.13; Microsoft shipped the fix in .NET 10.0.13 (SDK 10.0.113 and 10.0.402): https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/489, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md. The dotnet10-sdk package ships its own copies of System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll under /usr/lib/dotnet/sdk/<version>/ (the SDK root and FSharp directories), which the dotnet CLI, MSBuild, NuGet and F# tools load. Scanned every package built from the dotnet10-sdk source for Alpine 3.24 in the DHI Alpine repository (10.0.204-r0 to 10.0.303-r3, 8 builds; x86_64 and aarch64; including the -dbg, templates and doc subpackages, recursing into zip and NuGet archives) and read the version resources of every copy and the package versions recorded in the SDK's .deps.json files; both architectures match in every build. 10.0.204-r0, 10.0.301-r0, 10.0.302-r0, 10.0.302-r1 and 10.0.303-r0 carry System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 10.0.8 to 10.0.12 (assembly product versions 10.0.8 to 10.0.12), inside the affected range; 10.0.303-r1 and every later build carry 10.0.13 to 10.0.15 (the assemblies in 10.0.303-r1 report product version 10.0.13 although the SDK version is still 10.0.303), which include the fix; the 10.0.13 assembly is also larger than the 10.0.12 one.

CVE-2026-96959 (GHSA-c399-9853-6jmj) is a .NET denial of service issue in signed XML processing (System.Security.Cryptography.Xml and System.Private.Xml), classed as allocation of resources without limits (CWE-770). Microsoft's fix for this group of signed-XML issues adds input-depth and operation-count limits, prohibits DTD processing by default, validates entity references, bounds encrypted-data candidate processing and caps the attributes and namespaces used by C14N transforms. Microsoft lists System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 9.0.0 through 9.0.20 as affected on Windows, Linux and macOS, fixed in 9.0.21, and directs .NET 9.0 users to the 9.0.21 runtime; the .NET 9.0.21 release notes list this CVE (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c399-9853-6jmj, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/489, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.21/9.0.21.md). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold. Implementation copies of System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll are in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App shared framework (aspnetcore9-runtime, and the .NET SDK held by dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap), the SDK's own, F#, dotnet-format and dotnet watch copies and the ASP.NET Core runtime pack in dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap, and, in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts, the System.Security.Cryptography.Xml nupkg, the ASP.NET Core and WindowsDesktop transport nupkg files and the Arcade SDK build-tool nupkg. System.Private.Xml is in the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework, the runtime pack and the NativeAOT runtime pack, at each build's own .NET version. Each copy carries the build's own .NET version, except the Arcade SDK build-tool copy in the aarch64 9.0.21-r0 build, which is 9.0.20. So 9.0.12-r0 to 9.0.20-r0 and the aarch64 9.0.21-r0 package hold unfixed copies, and from 9.0.22-r0 on every copy is 9.0.21 or later. The other copies are reference assemblies with no implementation code. The range ends at 9.0.22-r0 because it is the first published build with no unfixed copy on either architecture; the x86_64 9.0.21-r0 package already holds only fixed copies.

Microsoft's fix for this group of signed-XML issues adds input-depth and operation-count limits, prohibits DTD processing by default, validates entity references, bounds encrypted-data candidate processing and caps the attributes and namespaces used by C14N transforms. Microsoft lists System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 9.0.0 through 9.0.20 as affected, fixed in 9.0.21; the .NET 9.0.21 release, which ships SDK 9.0.319 and 9.0.122, lists this CVE (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c399-9853-6jmj, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/489, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.21/9.0.21.md). We unpacked all 176 packages built from the DHI dotnet9-sdk source for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository, for x86_64 and aarch64 (dotnet9-sdk, dotnet9-sdk-aot, dotnet9-sdk-dbg, dotnet9-templates, netstandard21-targeting-pack, dotnet-doc and the bash and zsh completions), in the 11 published builds 9.0.113-r0, 9.0.114-r0, 9.0.115-r0, 9.0.116-r0, 9.0.117-r0, 9.0.118-r0, 9.0.119-r0, 9.0.121-r0, 9.0.122-r0, 9.0.123-r0 and 9.0.124-r0; each download matched the repository index checksum, and we opened the .nupkg and .zip archives inside them. dotnet9-sdk holds four implementation copies of System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll (the SDK directory, F#, dotnet-format and dotnet-watch), and dotnet9-sdk-aot holds one implementation copy of System.Private.Xml.dll in the native AOT compiler's framework directory (the Microsoft.DotNet.ILCompiler pack). dotnet9-sdk-dbg holds only debugging symbols (.pdb) for those System.Security.Cryptography.Xml copies, and no other package, and no archive inside one, holds either assembly. In every build on both architectures, every copy's product version is the .NET runtime version of that SDK release: 9.0.12 to 9.0.20 in the builds up to 9.0.121-r0, inside the affected range, and 9.0.21, 9.0.22 and 9.0.23 in 9.0.122-r0, 9.0.123-r0 and 9.0.124-r0, which contain the fix. The range ends at 9.0.122-r0.

CVE-2026-96959 (GHSA-c399-9853-6jmj): unbounded resource allocation in System.Security.Cryptography.Xml lets crafted signed or encrypted XML consume excessive resources and deny service. Microsoft fixed it in System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 10.0.13, shipped with .NET 10.0.13; versions 10.0.0 to 10.0.12 are affected (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-c399-9853-6jmj, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/489). DHI dotnet-sdk-10 for Debian 13 repackages Microsoft's .NET SDK. Unpacked every published dotnet-sdk-10 package in the DHI Debian repository, 10 builds from 10.0.301-0 to the current 10.0.404-1 for amd64 and arm64, including the .nupkg archives inside them, and read the file and product version of every copy of System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll; both architectures agree in every build. Each build carries copies in the ASP.NET Core shared framework (shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App), in the SDK directory and its FSharp directory, and a reference assembly in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref targeting pack, and in each build every copy has the same version: 10.0.9 in 10.0.301-0, 10.0.10 in 10.0.302-0 and 10.0.302-1, 10.0.11 in 10.0.400-1, 10.0.12 in 10.0.401-0 and 10.0.401-1, 10.0.13 in 10.0.402-0, 10.0.14 in 10.0.403-0, and 10.0.15 in 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1. No .nupkg archive in these packages contains it. The dotnet-sdk-10-oci-config packages from the same source hold only a configuration file and a changelog. So 10.0.402-0 is the first build with the fixed assembly, and every earlier build carries an affected version. The range ends at 10.0.402-0.
